nodes.statement: Let G be a Lie group, and let pi:P -> M be a principal G-bundle over a smooth manifold M. An Ehresmann connection zeta on pi assigns to every point p in P a vector subspace H_pP of T_pP such that: (1) T_pP = H_pP (+) V_pP where V_pP is the kernel of pi_*:T_pP -> T_{pi(p)}M; (2) for every g in G, writing g:P -> P for the action, g^*(H_pP) = H_{g.p}P. The subspaces H_pP and V_pP are the horizontal and vertical subspaces, respectively.

An Ehresmann connection on a principal G-bundle pi:P -> M can be regarded as a g-valued one-form tau on P, where g is the Lie algebra of G, defined via the fundamental vector fields X^A and the horizontal/vertical splitting, satisfying tau_p(X^A_p)=A, g^*(tau)=Ad_{g^{-1}} tau, and X_p in H_pP iff tau_p(X_p)=0.

A groupoid G is a category in which every morphism is invertible. The set of objects and the set of morphisms are denoted G_0 and G_1. Throughout, [G_1 => G_0] denotes a groupoid G with objects G_0 and morphisms G_1.

(Notation 5) Associated to a groupoid [G_1 => G_0] there are five structure maps: source s:G_1 -> G_0, target t:G_1 -> G_0, multiplication mult:G_1 x_{G_0} G_1 -> G_1 (composition of composable morphisms, with G_1 x_{G_0} G_1 the pullback of s and t), unit:G_0 -> G_1 sending x to 1_x, and inverse inv:G_1 -> G_1 sending h to h^{-1}.

A weak categorical group G is a weak monoidal category (M,(x),a,1,l,r) in which every morphism is invertible and each object x is weakly invertible, i.e. there exists an object x-bar with natural isomorphisms x (x) x-bar ~= 1 and x-bar (x) x ~= 1. Here 1 is the unit object, a the associator, and l,r the left and right unitors. Replacing all natural isomorphisms by identities yields strict monoidal categories and strict categorical groups; a strict categorical group is a strict monoidal groupoid.

A crossed module is a 4-tuple (G,H,alpha,beta) where: (1) G and H are groups, (2) beta:H -> G is a group homomorphism, (3) alpha:G x H -> H is an action of G on H, satisfying (Equivariance) beta(alpha(g,h)) = g.beta(h).g^{-1} and (Peiffer identity) alpha(beta(h),h') = h.h'.h^{-1}.
The notion of a crossed module extends naturally to topological crossed modules, in which the groups are topological groups and the associated maps are continuous.

Given a strict categorical group G one associates a crossed module (G,H,alpha,beta) with G:=Obj(G), H:=ker(s:Mor(G)->Obj(G)), alpha(g,h):=id_g (x) h (x) id_{g^{-1}}, and beta the restriction of the target map to H. Conversely, from a crossed module one constructs a strict categorical group with Obj=G, Mor=H |x G, s(h,g)=g, t(h,g)=beta(h).g, composition (h',beta(h).g)o(h,g)=(h'.h,g), tensor g (x) g' = g.g' and (h,g)(x)(h',g') = (h.alpha(g,h'), g.g').

Ganter's categorical circle U(1) is the strict categorical group associated to the crossed module (R, Z x R/Z, alpha, beta), where alpha(r,(m,[a]))=(m,[a+rm]) and beta(m,[a])=m; objects R, morphisms (Z x R/Z) |x R, with s((m,[a]),r)=r, t((m,[a]),r)=r+m, and tensor multiplication ((m,[a]),r)(x)((n,[b]),s)=((m+n,[a+b+rn]),r+s).
A categorical space M is a category for which Obj(M) and Mor(M) are topological spaces and all structure maps are continuous. We write M_0 and M_1 for Obj(M) and Mor(M).
A topological space M may be regarded as a categorical space whose objects are the points of M and whose only morphisms are identities, so Obj(M)=M and Mor(M)=M.

Let M, M' be categorical spaces. A continuous categorical map F:M -> M' is a functor such that F_0:M_0 -> M'_0 and F_1:M_1 -> M'_1 are continuous. If there exists a functor F-bar:M' -> M together with continuous natural transformations F o F-bar => id_{M'} and F-bar o F => id_M, then F is an equivalence of categorical spaces and F-bar a weak inverse of F.

Let M be a topological space regarded as a categorical space and G a strict categorical group. M is a categorical right G-space if there exists a continuous categorical map epsilon:M x G -> M such that the action-associativity diagram commutes, where m_G is the tensor multiplication of G.

Let G be a strict categorical group and M a smooth manifold. A principal G-bundle over M is a categorical right G-space P together with a G-equivariant map rho:P -> M such that the smooth functor (pr_1,R):P x G -> P x_M P is a weak equivalence, where R is the right action of G on P.

Waldorf's Definition 1.8 is generally restrictive since it requires local trivialisations given by strong equivalences, but this does not affect the essential features of the constructions here; where greater generality is needed one passes to Waldorf's formulation admitting anafunctors in place of strict functors.

Let X be a topological space and G a strict categorical group with associated crossed module (G,H,alpha,beta). A G-valued cocycle on X is a triple (W_i,g_ij,h_ijk) where {W_i} is an open cover of X and for each i,j,k the maps g_ij:W_i ^ W_j -> G and h_ijk:W_i ^ W_j ^ W_k -> H are smooth, satisfying pointwise: g_ii = e_G; beta(h_ijk).g_ij.g_jk = g_ik; h_ijj = h_jji = e_H; h_ijk.h_ikl = h_ijl.alpha(g_ij,h_jkl).

Given a G-valued cocycle (W_i,g_ij,h_ijk) on X one constructs a principal G-bundle rho:P -> X with Obj(P)=union_i (W_i x G), Mor(P)=union_{i,j}((W_i^W_j) x H x G), source s(w,h,g)=(w,g), target t(w,h,g)=(w, g_ij(w)^{-1}.beta(h).g), explicit composition, the action (w,g).g'=(w,g.g') and (w,h,g).(h',g')=(w,h.alpha(g,h'),g.g'), and trivialisations phi_i.
(Notation 19) The disjoint unions for Obj(P) and Mor(P) are written Obj(P)=U_i({i} x W_i x G) and Mor(P)=U_{i,j}({(i,j)} x (W_i^W_j) x H x G), so an object is (i,w,g) and a morphism is (i,j,w,h,g).

Let P be a categorical space and Gamma a strict categorical Lie group with crossed module (G,H,alpha,beta) and categorical Lie algebra (g,h,alpha_*,beta_*). A gamma-valued k-form Psi consists of Psi^a in Omega^k(P_0,g), Psi^b in Omega^k(P_1,h), Psi^c in Omega^{k+1}(P_0,h). The differential D:Omega^k(P,gamma) -> Omega^{k+1}(P,gamma) has components (DPsi)^a = dPsi^a - (-1)^k t_*(Psi^c), (DPsi)^b = dPsi^b - (-1)^k Delta(Psi^c), (DPsi)^c = dPsi^c.

Let Gamma be a categorical Lie group with categorical Lie algebra gamma and rho:P -> M a principal Gamma-bundle, with action R:P x Gamma -> P and crossed module (G,H,alpha,beta). A connection Omega on rho is a gamma-valued 1-form on P satisfying R^* Omega = Ad^{-1}_{pr_Gamma}(pr^*_P Omega) + pr^*_Gamma theta, where pr_Gamma, pr_P are the projections and theta is the Maurer-Cartan form on Gamma. The curvature curv(Omega) is a 2-form in Omega^2(P,gamma).

Two extreme cases of a connection on a categorical bundle: (1) Gamma = G an ordinary group recovers the usual notion of connection on a principal bundle; (2) Gamma = BU(1) gives a connection on a bundle gerbe.
There is a natural correspondence between complex line bundles and principal U(1)-bundles, used interchangeably throughout.
(Notation 24) For pi:Y -> M continuous, Y^[k] denotes the k-fold fibre product Y x_M ... x_M Y (k times), and pi_ij:Y^[3] -> Y^[2] the projection onto the i-th and j-th factors.

Let M be a smooth manifold. A bundle gerbe over M is a triple (L,Y,M) consisting of a surjective submersion pi:Y -> M, a line bundle lambda:L -> Y^[2], and an isomorphism m:pi_12^*L (x) pi_23^*L -> pi_13^*L (the bundle gerbe product) such that the associativity diagram L_{(y1,y2)}(x)L_{(y2,y3)}(x)L_{(y3,y4)} commutes for each (y1,y2,y3,y4) in Y^[4].

Construction one for the basic bundle gerbe over S^3: with W = S^3 minus {(0,0,0,-1)} and W' = S^3 minus {(0,0,0,1)}, whose intersection is homotopy equivalent to S^2, the bundle gerbe (L,Y,S^3) has Y = W u W', line bundle L -> Y^[2] trivial over W and W' and equal over W^W' to the pullback along the canonical map f of the line bundle of the Hopf map (representing class 1 in H^2(S^2;Z)), and bundle gerbe product defined case by case on triple intersections.

Construction two for the basic bundle gerbe over S^3: with V_N = S^2 minus {(0,0,-1)}, V_S = S^2 minus {(0,0,1)} and W_N = eta^{-1}(V_N), W_S = eta^{-1}(V_S) covering S^3, where W_N^W_S ~ T^2, the bundle gerbe (L,Y,S^3) has Y = W_N u W_S, trivial line bundles over W_N, W_S, and over W_N^W_S the pullback along f of the quotient line bundle (R^2 x C)/~ with ((x,y),e)~((x+m,y+n),e^{2pi i my}.e).

Let M be a smooth manifold. (1) Given a principal BU(1)-bundle rho:P -> M one constructs a bundle gerbe (L,Y,M): take Y=Obj(P), pi=rho_0, P=Mor(P), and lambda=(s,t):P -> Y^[2], showing lambda defines a principal U(1)-bundle (hence a line bundle L over Y^[2]) and defining the gerbe product m over triple intersections. (2) Conversely, from a bundle gerbe (L,Y,M) one constructs a BU(1)-bundle rho:P -> M with Obj(P)=Y, Mor(P)=L, source/target via lambda, composition via the gerbe product m, identity via the diagonal pullback, and the natural U(1)-action on L.

Let (L,Y,M) be a bundle gerbe. A connection and curving consist of: (1) a connection nabla on the line bundle L -> Y^[2]; (2) an associative isomorphism m_nabla:pi_12^*(L,nabla) (x) pi_23^*(L,nabla) -> pi_13^*(L,nabla) compatible with the gerbe product; (3) a 2-form C in Omega^2(Y) (the curving) satisfying pi_2^*C - pi_1^*C = R_nabla, with R_nabla the curvature of nabla. There exists a unique 3-form D on M with pi^*D = dC.

Let M be a manifold with open cover {U_i}. A cocycle for a bundle gerbe (L,Y,M) is a triple (g_ijk,A_ij,B_i) where g_ijk is a smooth U(1)-valued function on U_i^U_j^U_k, A_ij a 1-form on U_i^U_j, B_i a 2-form on U_i, satisfying g_ijk.g_ikl = g_jkl.g_ijl, A_ik = A_ij + A_jk + (1/i)g_ijk^{-1}dg_ijk, dA_ij = B_j - B_i.

From local sections s_i:U_i -> Y of a bundle gerbe one obtains transition functions g_ijk:U_i^U_j^U_k -> U(1) via m(delta_ij(x),delta_jk(x)) = g_ijk(x) delta_ik(x), and with a connection/curving the forms A_ij, B_i, giving a cocycle (g_ijk,A_ij,B_i). Without connection/curving [g_ijk] lies in Cech H^2(M, U(1)) and maps to the Dixmier-Douady class in H^3(M;Z); with connection/curving one obtains a class in Deligne cohomology.

(Observation 32) The bundle gerbes in Examples 26 (murbun) and 27 (ourbun) are equivalent: each has Dixmier-Douady class 1 in H^3(S^3;Z), the positive generator, obtained via the connecting homomorphism in the Mayer-Vietoris sequence from the line bundle class 1 in H^2(W^W';Z).

Let U be the Cech groupoid associated with the open cover {U_1,U_2,U_3,U_4} of S^1, where U_1={(X,Y) in S^1 | X>0}, U_2={X<0}, U_3={Y>0}, U_4={Y<0}. Objects: U_1 u U_2 u U_3 u U_4; arrows: the non-empty pairwise intersections; with s(i,j,(X,Y))=(i,(X,Y)) and t(i,j,(X,Y))=(j,(X,Y)).

Let G be a group acting on a topological space X from the left. The action groupoid [G x X => X] has object set X and morphism set G x X; the source map is projection to the first factor, the target map is the action G x X -> X, and composition is induced by multiplication in G.

(Construction 36) A groupoid homomorphism U -> U(1) is built as phi o kappa, where phi:[Z x R => R] -> U(1) is given by phi_0:r |-> r and phi_1:(m,r) |-> ((m,[r]),r), and kappa:U -> [Z x R => R] is defined on objects via arcsin/arccos branch formulas on each U_i and on morphisms by the corresponding integer-and-real pairs, making the diagram with p and q commute.

Once kappa_0 is defined, kappa_1 is determined by it since the source, target, and their images under kappa_0 are known; the integers in kappa_1 are the differences of targets and sources. The ranges of arcsin and arccos are taken to be (-pi/2, pi/2) and (0, pi).
The morphism phi, defined in Construction 36 (phiandkappa), is a groupoid homomorphism.

::: proof
*Proof.* We need to show that $\phi$ preserves all structure maps $\mathsf{s}$, $\mathsf{t}$, $\mathsf{mult}$, $\mathsf{unit}$ and $\mathsf{inv}$. [explicit computations for source, target, multiplication, unit, inverse] So, $\phi$ preserves the inverse map. QED
:::
nodes.statement: Proof. We show that phi preserves all structure maps s, t, mult, unit, inv. Direct computation gives phi_0(s(m,r))=r=s(phi_1(m,r)); phi_0(t(m,r))=r+m=t(phi_1(m,r)); phi_1((n,r+m)o(m,r))=((m+n,[r]),r)=phi_1(n,r+m)o phi_1(m,r); phi_1(unit(r))=((0,[r]),r)=unit(phi_0(r)); phi_1(inv(m,r))=((-m,[r+m]),r+m)=inv(phi_1(m,r)). Hence phi is a groupoid homomorphism.
The morphism kappa, defined in Construction 36 (phiandkappa), is a groupoid homomorphism.

::: proof
*Proof.* Here, it suffices to verify that $\kappa$ preserves all structure maps $\mathsf{s}$, $\mathsf{t}$, $\mathsf{mult}$, $\mathsf{unit}$ and $\mathsf{inv}$. We carry out the check for objects in $U_2$ and $U_3$, and for arrows in $U_2 \cap U_3$; the remaining cases are analogous. [computations] So, $\kappa$ preserves the inverse map. QED
:::
nodes.statement: Proof. It suffices to verify that kappa preserves s, t, mult, unit, inv. The check is carried out for objects in U_2 and U_3 and arrows in U_2^U_3 (the remaining cases analogous): kappa_0(s(X,Y))=arcsin(-Y)/2pi+1/2=s(kappa_1(X,Y)); kappa_0(t(X,Y))=arccos(X)/2pi=t(kappa_1(X,Y)); kappa_1 respects composition, unit, and inverse. Hence kappa is a groupoid homomorphism.

(Construction 39) Using the six-open cover {V_1,...,V_6} of S^2 (V_1={X>0}, V_2={X<0}, V_3={Y>0}, V_4={Y<0}, V_5={Z>0}, V_6={Z<0}) and the map sigma:(X,Y,Z) |-> (X,Y)/sqrt(X^2+Y^2), the smooth maps g_ij:V_i^V_j -> R and h_ijk:V_i^V_j^V_k -> Z x R/Z (built from phi_0,kappa_0,sigma and phi_1,kappa_1,sigma) form a U(1)-valued cocycle. The resulting total 2-space P (Obj = union_i V_i x R, Mor = union_{i,j}((V_i^V_j) x (Z x R/Z) x R)) with projection rho:P -> S^2 and the action of U(1) defines a principal U(1)-bundle rho:P -> S^2, the categorical Hopf map.

Let F:G -> G' be a map of strict categorical groups, and let F~:(G,H,alpha,beta) -> (G',H',alpha',beta') denote the induced map between the associated crossed modules. Let X be a topological space and (W_i,g_ij,h_ijk) the G-valued cocycle of a principal G-bundle over X. Then composing g_ij:W_i^W_j -> G with F~_0:G -> G', and h_ijk:W_i^W_j^W_k -> H with F~_1:H -> H', yields a principal G'-bundle over X.

nodes.source_tex:
::: proof
*Proof.* Define $g^\prime_{ij} = \widetilde{F}_0 \circ g_{ij}$, $h^\prime_{ijk} = \widetilde{F}_1 \circ h_{ijk}$. We verify the cocycle conditions for a $\mathcal{G}^\prime$-bundle: $g^\prime_{ii} = e_{G^\prime}$, $\beta(h^\prime_{ijk}) \cdot g^\prime_{ij} \cdot g^\prime_{jk} = g^\prime_{ik}$, $h^\prime_{ijj} = h^\prime_{jji} = e_{H^\prime}$, $h^\prime_{ijk} \cdot h^\prime_{ikl} = \alpha(g^\prime_{ij},h^\prime_{jkl}) \cdot h^\prime_{ijl}$. Since $\widetilde{F}$ is a crossed module homomorphism, these follow by applying $\widetilde{F}_0$ to Equations (gii),(cocycleg) and $\widetilde{F}_1$ to (hijj),(cocycleh). QED
:::
nodes.statement: Proof. Define g'_ij = F~_0 o g_ij and h'_ijk = F~_1 o h_ijk. These satisfy the cocycle conditions for a G'-bundle: g'_ii = e_{G'}; beta(h'_ijk).g'_ij.g'_jk = g'_ik; h'_ijj = h'_jji = e_{H'}; h'_ijk.h'_ikl = alpha(g'_ij,h'_jkl).h'_ijl. Since F~ is a crossed module homomorphism, these follow by applying F~_0 to Equations (gii),(cocycleg) and F~_1 to (hijj),(cocycleh). Hence the claim follows.

Let G be a group, viewed as a strict categorical group G with objects G and only identity morphisms. Let X be a topological space with an open cover {W_i}. Then constructing a principal G-bundle over X (in the categorical sense) yields a principal G-bundle over X.

nodes.source_tex:
::: proof
*Proof.* Since both the object and morphism groups of $\mathcal{G}$ are $G$, the crossed module is $(G,\{\mathbbm{1}\},\alpha,\beta)$ with trivial $\alpha,\beta$. Consider smooth maps $g_{ij}:W_i\cap W_j\to G$, $h_{ijk}\to\{\mathbbm{1}\}$ satisfying (gii),(cocycleg),(hijj),(cocycleh) of Definition (gvaluedcocycle). Construct $\mathcal{Q}$ with $\mathsf{Obj}=\sqcup_i(W_i\times G)$, $\mathsf{Mor}=\sqcup_{i,j}((W_i\cap W_j)\times\{\mathbbm{1}\}\times G)$; an arrow gives $g'=g^{-1}_{ij}(w)\cdot g$, i.e. $g=g_{ij}\cdot g'$. Since $g_{ij}\cdot g_{jk}=g_{ik}$, $(W_i,g_{ij})$ defines a principal $G$-bundle over $X$. QED
:::
nodes.statement: Proof. Since the object and morphism groups of G are both G, the associated crossed module is (G,{1},alpha,beta) with trivial alpha,beta. Consider smooth maps g_ij:W_i^W_j -> G and h_ijk:W_i^W_j^W_k -> {1} satisfying cocycle conditions (gii),(cocycleg),(hijj),(cocycleh) of Definition 17 (gvaluedcocycle). Construct the total categorical space Q with Obj = union_i (W_i x G), Mor = union_{i,j}((W_i^W_j) x {1} x G); an arrow (w,1,g) -> (w,g') has g' = g_ij^{-1}(w).g, equivalently g = g_ij.g'. Since the g_ij satisfy g_ij.g_jk = g_ik, the collection (W_i,g_ij) defines transition functions of a principal G-bundle over X.
Define F~_0:R -> S^1 and F~_1:Z x R/Z -> {1} by F~_0:r |-> q_0(r) = (cos(2 pi r), sin(2 pi r)) and F~_1:(m,[a]) |-> 1.

Take the cover of S^2 as in Construction 39 (cathopf), and let g_ij and h_ijk be the smooth maps defined therein. Then g'_ij = F~_0 o g_ij and h'_ijk = F~_1 o h_ijk determine the transition data of the Hopf map eta:S^3 -> S^2.

::: proof
*Proof.* By Lemmas (priGtoG') and (primathGtoG), the maps $g^\prime_{ij}$ and $h^\prime_{ijk}$ provide the cocycle data for a principal $U(1)$-bundle over $S^2$. It suffices to show the associated total categorical space $\mathcal{Q}$ is equivalent to $S^3$. Reconstructing $\eta$ with $U(1)$ as a strict categorical group gives $\widetilde{\eta}:\mathcal{Q}'\to S^2$ over $\{V_N,V_S\}$, with $\mathcal{Q}'\simeq S^3$. By [Waldorf Def 2.20, Thm 2.22] a semi-strict bundle morphism $\mathcal{Q}'\to\mathcal{Q}$ (trivial on objects and morphisms) yields the Morita equivalence $\mathcal{Q}\leftarrow \mathcal{Q}'\rightarrow S^3$. QED
:::
nodes.statement: Proof. By Lemmas 40 (priGtoG') and 41 (primathGtoG), g'_ij and h'_ijk are cocycle data for a principal U(1)-bundle over S^2; it suffices to show the associated total categorical space Q (Obj = union_i(V_i x S^1), Mor = union_{i,j}((V_i^V_j) x {1} x S^1)) is equivalent to S^3. Reconstructing eta with U(1) as a strict categorical group gives a categorical bundle eta~:Q' -> S^2 over the cover {V_N,V_S}; Q' is equivalent to S^3 as a categorical space. It remains to show Q ~ Q', via a semi-strict bundle morphism Q' -> Q (Waldorf Def 2.20, Thm 2.22), defined trivially on objects and morphisms, yielding the Morita equivalence Q <- Q' -> S^3.

Consider the action of BU(1) on the total categorical space P of the categorical Hopf map, P x BU(1) -> P, given on objects by ((v,r),1) |-> (v,r) and on morphisms by ((v,(m,[a]),r),[b]) |-> (v,(m,[a+b]),r). Then the quotient categorical space P/BU(1) is equivalent, as a categorical space, to S^3.

nodes.source_tex:
::: proof
*Proof.* Write $\mathcal{Q}^{\prime\prime} = \mathcal{P}/\mathbb{B}U(1)$, with objects $\sqcup_i (V_i \times \mathbb{R})$ and morphisms $\sqcup_{i,j}((V_i \cap V_j) \times \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{R})$. By Proposition (giveHopf) and the equivalence of $[\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{R} \rightrightarrows \mathbb{R}]$ with $[S^1 \rightrightarrows S^1]$, $\mathcal{Q}^{\prime\prime}$ presents $S^3$. Hence $\mathcal{P}/\mathbb{B}U(1) \simeq S^3$. QED
:::
nodes.statement: Proof. Write Q'' = P/BU(1). Then Obj(Q'') = union_i (V_i x R) and Mor(Q'') = union_{i,j}((V_i^V_j) x Z x R). By Proposition 43 (giveHopf) and the fact that the action groupoid [Z x R => R] is equivalent to [S^1 => S^1], Q'' presents the same categorical space as the total space of the Hopf map, namely S^3. Hence P/BU(1) ~ S^3 as categorical spaces.

The object space of the categorical bundle is Y = union_i (V_i x R); from this one constructs the basic bundle gerbe over S^3 using the cover {V_i x S^1}_{i=1}^6 of S^3 by six solid tori, embedded via local sections of the Hopf map f_i(v,z)=s_i(v).z. Then Y^[2] = union_{i,j}((V_i^V_j) x R x Z) and the associated U(1)-bundle L over Y^[2] is L = union_{i,j}((V_i x V_j) x R x Z x S^1); the categorical space Q'' of Prop 44 is equivalent to Y with Obj(Y)=Y, Mor(Y)=Y x_{S^3} Y.
(Observation 46) The categorical space Q in Proposition 43 (giveHopf) is equivalent to the categorical space Q'' in Proposition 44 (modbu), by arguments similar to the proof of Proposition 43.
(Observation 47) The map H~:P -> P/BU(1), defined on objects by H~_0(v,r)=(v,r) and on morphisms by H~_1((v,(m,[a])),r)=(v,m,r), is a non-trivial principal BU(1)-bundle.

::: proof
*Proof.* By Remark (butobunandconv), it suffices to show the associated bundle gerbe $(L,Y,S^3)$ is non-trivial. $Y = \mathsf{Obj}(\mathcal{P}) = \sqcup_i (V_i \times \mathbb{R})$ with $\pi:Y\to S^3$ as in Remark (spacey2andl); $L = \mathsf{Mor}(\mathcal{P})$, $\lambda(v,(m,[a]),r)=((v,r),(v,r+m))$; the gerbe product is defined case by case as in Remark (butobunandconv). Taking the cover $\{V_i\times S^1\}_{i=1}^6$ and local sections gives $m(\delta_{14},\delta_{45})=g_{145}\delta_{15}$, a class $[g]\in\check{H}^2(S^3,\underline{U(1)})$; the connecting homomorphism (Snake lemma) sends $[g]$ to $1\in H^3(S^3;\mathbb{Z})$. Hence the gerbe is non-trivial. The construction of $g_{145}$ depends on the morphisms and compositions in $\mathcal{P}$, as in Construction (cathopf). QED
:::
nodes.statement: Proof. By Remark 28 (butobunandconv), it suffices to show the associated bundle gerbe (L,Y,S^3) is non-trivial. With Y = Obj(P) = union_i (V_i x R) and projection pi:Y -> S^3 as in Remark 45 (spacey2andl), L = Mor(P) = union_{i,j}((V_i^V_j) x (Z x R/Z) x R), and lambda(v,(m,[a]),r) = ((v,r),(v,r+m)); the gerbe product is defined case by case as in Remark 28. Taking the cover {V_i x S^1} of S^3 and local sections sec_1, sec_4, sec_5 yields maps s_14, s_45, s_15, pulled-back line bundles L_14, L_45, L_15, and unit sections delta giving m(delta_14,delta_45) = g_145 delta_15 for a U(1)-valued function g_145. This determines a class [g] in Cech H^2(S^3, U(1)); the connecting homomorphism (via the Snake lemma) sends [g] to 1 in H^3(S^3;Z). Hence the bundle gerbe is non-trivial. The construction of g_145 depends on the morphisms and compositions in P, as in Construction 39 (cathopf).

(Observation 48) The bundle gerbes of Examples 26 (murbun) and 27 (ourbun), together with the bundle gerbe arising in Observation 47 (mapH), are all equivalent: their Dixmier-Douady classes coincide, each representing the generator 1 in H^3(S^3;Z).

Considering eta:S^3 -> S^2, rho:P -> S^2 and H~:P -> P/BU(1), there is a commutative factorization diagram in which P -> P/BU(1) ~ S^3 -> S^2 with eta~ the categorical bundle of structure group U(1) associated to eta; H is the composite of the equivalence P/BU(1) ~ S^3 with H~, and both H and H~ yield equivalent constructions of the basic bundle gerbe over S^3.

(Observation 50) The map rho:P -> S^2 defines a non-trivial principal U(1)-bundle. Using the exact sequence of categorical groups 1 -> BU(1) -> U(1) -> U(1) -> 1 (classified in H^3_{SM}(U(1);Z) ~= H^4(BU(1);Z) ~= Z) and the induced diagram of classifying spaces, the categorical Hopf map is a lift of the Hopf map, so Cech H^1(S^2, U(1)) ~= Z and the associated principal U(1)-bundle is non-trivial, classified by the positive generator 1.
By symmetries of the Hopf map we mean pairs (A,psi) with A in SO(3) and psi:S^3 -> S^3 such that the square (eta, A, eta) commutes and psi preserves the chosen Ehresmann connection on eta.

Let M be a simply-connected smooth manifold and omega/2pi an integral closed 2-form on M. (i) There exists a principal U(1)-bundle pi:P -> M with a connection zeta whose curvature is omega. (ii) Given two principal U(1)-bundles pi:P -> M and pi':P' -> M with connections zeta and zeta' having the same curvature omega, there exists a morphism psi:P -> P' of principal U(1)-bundles such that [psi^*zeta'] = [zeta]; moreover psi is unique up to multiplication by elements of U(1).

Let G be a Lie group acting smoothly on a simply-connected smooth manifold M, leaving an integral closed 2-form omega/2pi on M invariant. Then there exists a central extension G~ of G by U(1) canonically associated to the pair (M,omega).
Following Propositions 52 and 53, Pressley and Segal present three equivalent constructions of the extension G~; the categorical analogues of these constructions are given at the end of the section.

(Construction 55) Specialising Propositions 53 and 52 to M=S^2, P=S^3, G=U(1), pi=eta, with the SO(3)-invariant volume form omega' on S^2 and connection 1-form zeta = -ydx + xdy - wdz + zdw on S^3 (curvature omega = omega'/2), one realises SO(3)~ as pairs (A,psi) with A in SO(3) and psi:S^3 -> A^*S^3 a U(1)-bundle morphism, identified with the fibre product {(A,b') in SO(3) x S^3 | eta(b')=A Y_N}. Since H^2_{SM}(SO(3);U(1)) ~= Z_2, the non-trivial central extension is Spin^c(3); a D_8 sub-extension argument shows SO(3)~ is neither homeomorphic nor isomorphic to SO(3) x U(1).
The connection zeta defined in Equation (connonHopf), zeta = -ydx + xdy - wdz + zdw, is invariant under multiplication by elements of S^3.

nodes.source_tex:
::: proof
*Proof.* Let $(x_0,y_0,z_0,w_0) \in S^3$. Identifying $S^3$ with the unit quaternions, the product of $(x,y,z,w)$ with $(x_0,y_0,z_0,w_0)$ is computed explicitly. Substituting into the connection one-form $\zeta$ and collecting coefficients of $dx$ yields $-y$; the coefficients of $dy$, $dz$, $dw$ are verified similarly. Thus $\zeta$ is preserved under multiplication by elements of $S^3$. QED
:::
nodes.statement: Proof. Let (x0,y0,z0,w0) in S^3. Identifying S^3 with the unit quaternions, the product of (x,y,z,w) with (x0,y0,z0,w0) is computed explicitly. Substituting into zeta and collecting the coefficient of dx gives -y, and the coefficients of dy, dz, dw are verified by similar calculations. Thus zeta is preserved under multiplication by elements of S^3.

The connection zeta on the Hopf map eta:S^3 -> S^2 arises naturally: pulling back a primitive alpha of the restricted 2-form omega = (1/2)(XdY^dZ + YdZ^dX + ZdX^dY) on the upper hemisphere along eta gives eta^*alpha = (-ydx+xdy)/(x^2+y^2) + (ydx-xdy) + (wdz-zdw), which differs from zeta by the exact 1-form (-ydx+xdy)/(x^2+y^2); hence [zeta] = [eta^*alpha].
The group of symmetries of the Hopf map eta:S^3 -> S^2 is isomorphic to Spin^c(3).

*Proof.* This follows directly from Construction (symmofhopf) and statement (ii) in Proposition (secondprop). QED

Let M be a 2-connected smooth manifold with an integral closed 3-form nu/2pi^2. (1) There exists a principal BU(1)-bundle J:Q -> M with a connection Omega whose curvature is nu. (2) Given two principal BU(1)-bundles J:Q -> M and J':Q' -> M with connections Omega and Omega' having the same curvature nu, there exists an anafunctor Psi:Q -> Q' such that [Psi^*Omega'] = [Omega]; moreover Psi is unique up to a transformation, which is unique up to multiplication by elements of U(1).

nodes.source_tex:
::: proof
*Proof.* Both statements follow from the classification of bundle gerbes over $M$ by $H^3(S^3;\mathbb{Z})$ and the fact that $\nu/2\pi^2$ represents the image of a third integral cohomology class in real cohomology. The uniqueness of a transformation between two such anafunctors $\mathcal{Q} \to \mathcal{Q}$ is established using [MR2318389 Corollary 2.3]: the set of isomorphism classes of 1-morphisms forms a torsor over the isomorphism classes of line bundles over $M$, and since $H^2(M;\mathbb{Z}) = 0$ the result follows. QED
:::
nodes.statement: Proof. Both statements follow from the classification of bundle gerbes over M by H^3(S^3;Z) and the fact that nu/2pi^2 represents the image of a third integral cohomology class in real cohomology. The uniqueness of a transformation between two such anafunctors Q -> Q is established using [MR2318389 Corollary 2.3]: the set of isomorphism classes of 1-morphisms forms a torsor over the isomorphism classes of line bundles over M, and since H^2(M;Z)=0 the result follows.

Let M be a 2-connected smooth manifold with an integral closed 3-form nu/2pi^2, and let G be a Lie group acting on M leaving nu/2pi^2 invariant. Given a principal BU(1)-bundle J:Q -> M with a connection Omega whose curvature is nu, there exists an anafunctor Phi:Q -> Q covering the action of G on M such that [Phi^*Omega] = [Omega].

nodes.source_tex:
::: proof
*Proof.* Let $g \in G$. The action of $g$ gives a map $g:M \to M$ and a pullback $g^\ast J:g^\ast \mathcal{Q} \to M$. By Proposition (secondpropcat) there is a connection-preserving anafunctor $\Psi:\mathcal{Q} \to g^\ast \mathcal{Q}$. Considering the pullback square over $g$ and setting $\Phi = \lambda \circ \Psi$, then $(\lambda \circ \Psi)^\ast \Omega = \Psi^\ast (g^\ast \Omega) = \Omega$, and $\Phi$ makes the square commute. QED
:::
nodes.statement: Proof. Let g in G. The action of g gives a map g:M -> M and a pullback g^*J:g^*Q -> M of J along g. By Proposition 59 (secondpropcat) there is a connection-preserving anafunctor Psi:Q -> g^*Q fitting into a commutative triangle over M. Considering the pullback square (g^*Q, lambda, Q, J) over g, define Phi = lambda o Psi. Then (lambda o Psi)^*Omega = Psi^*(g^*Omega) = Omega, and Phi makes the square (J, Phi, J, g) commute.

By Proposition 59 (secondpropcat) one obtains a principal BU(1)-bundle J:Q -> M and defines a categorical group CG with objects pairs (g,Psi) (g in G, Psi:Q -> Q an anafunctor from Corollary 60) and morphisms transformations F:(g,Psi) -> (g,Psi'); tensor products via composition of anafunctors and of transformations. A conjectural map P G -> CG (with P G the Lie 2-group model of String(n) at k=1) is described using the parallel 2-transport formalism.

(Construction 62, conjectural) Specialising Proposition 59 (secondpropcat) to G = Spin(3), M = S^3, J = H:P -> S^3, with S^3 equipped with the volume form nu = xdy^dz^dw + ydz^dw^dx + zdw^dx^dy + wdx^dy^dz (integral 2pi^2, so nu/2pi^2 generates H^3(S^3;Z) and corresponds to the basic bundle gerbe). Equipping this gerbe with a connection Omega of curvature nu and adapting Construction 55 yields the categorical group CSpin(3), with objects pairs (g,Psi) (g in Spin(3), Psi:P -> P an anafunctor covering g and preserving the connection on H) and morphisms transformations F:(g,Psi) -> (g,Psi'); a new interpretation of String(3).

In the conjectural Construction 62, the aim is to generalise the constructions of Pressley-Segal, focusing on describing the categorical group String(3) as the categorical group of symmetries of the categorical Hopf map.

The Hopf map eta(x,y,z,w) = (2(xz+yw), 2(yz-xw), -x^2-y^2+z^2+w^2) arises from q k q-bar with q = x + y i + z j + w k. Its kernel is K = {(0,0,sin t, cos t) in S^3 | t in R} = cos t + sin t k, with base-point (0,0,1) in S^2.

For omega = (1/2)(XdY^dZ + YdZ^dX + ZdX^dY) on S^2 and zeta = -ydx + xdy - wdz + zdw on S^3, with eta the Hopf map, a direct computation of eta^*omega coefficient-by-coefficient, using xdx+ydy+zdz+wdw=0 on S^3, gives eta^*omega = 2dx^dy + 2dz^dw = d zeta.

(Construction 69) An alternative four-open cover {X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4} of S^2 obtained from spherical projections of the faces of an inscribed tetrahedron, compatible with the tetrahedral group Tet action; X_1 = {(X,Y,Z) in S^2 | z < epsilon} and X_2, X_3, X_4 neighbourhoods of the projected faces described in spherical coordinates by theta-ranges of width 2pi/3 and phi < 2pi/3 (with epsilon > 0).

theorem_candidates.statement: Let M be a 2-connected smooth manifold with an integral closed 3-form nu/2pi^2. (1) There exists a principal BU(1)-bundle J:Q -> M with a connection Omega whose curvature is nu. (2) Given two principal BU(1)-bundles J:Q -> M and J':Q' -> M with connections Omega and Omega' having the same curvature nu, there exists an anafunctor Psi:Q -> Q' such that [Psi^*Omega'] = [Omega]; moreover Psi is unique up to a transformation, which is unique up to multiplication by elements of U(1).
